pr_title: Logging added for when compaction takes more than the block time range
pr_comments:
I think that'd be over complicating things, this isn't meant to be 100% precise. A single head compaction taking more than 2h is enough to check for.

The log message is also not quite right. The block compaction did finish (we wouldn't know how long it took otherwise), and I don't think it's wise to advise users to blow away good data.

> A single head compaction taking more than 2h is enough to check for.

It is mostly the checkpointing that takes time, compacting Head into a block won't take that long.
Did you mean the entire head compaction where we would compact multiple blocks out of Head?
No, only one block as that's the usual case. For simplicity let's presume that we've not fallen a block behind already.

> Things are a little more tricky now. WAL truncation + checkpoint happens in `Compact()` now and not here.

Didn't know that, thanks for the info!

> The log message is also not quite right. The block compaction did finish (we wouldn't know how long it took otherwise), and I don't think it's wise to advise users to blow away good data.

What would be the best advice here? Ask the user for more resources? Delete something more specific?

> I think that'd be over complicating things, this isn't meant to be 100% precise. A single head compaction taking more than 2h is enough to check for.

I'm a little confused with when to log...  
`(all compaction durations + wal truncation duration) > (lastBlockMaxT-firstBlockMinT)`, is that correct?

> What would be the best advice here? Ask the user for more resources? Delete something more specific?

We shouldn't be giving any advice like this in a log message. It's a warning, not an operational manual.
Hello :wave:, anything else I should be adjusting here?

issue_context.title: Improve logging to report point of no return during checkpointing due to overload
issue_context.body:
**What did you do?**

We run two instances of Prometheus. This pod filled its volume. After expanding the volume the process was continually OOM killed after starting and replaying the WAL. All the while the other instance was running fine. I stopped scraping goldpinger and was able to get past that OOM event and see it enter a loop of Head GC and WAL checkpointing. The checkpoints appear to be getting larger each time. The process did eventually get OOM killed after several hours and started the checkpoint cycle over again.

**What did you expect to see?**

Prometheus recover and match the curve of the other instance.

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**

Checkpoints grow in size. Prometheus never settles into normal disk usage.

**Environment**

* System information:

	Linux 5.5.5-200.fc31.x86_64 x86_64

* Prometheus version:

	prometheus, version 2.19.1 (branch: HEAD, revision: eba3fdcbf0d378b66600281903e3aab515732b39)
	build user:       root@62700b3d0ef9
	build date:       20200618-16:35:26
	go version:       go1.14.4

comments:
If possible I'd like to get more info on how to recover from this state. I eventually removed the contents of the `wal` directory. That appears to have righted this process.

More documentation around the directory structure would be helpful.

There is no mention of the chunks_head directory.

The docs mention blowing away the entire data directory. In our case, removing the contents of the wal directory was enough to recover.
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/7579 could partially help here to get rid of a loop of WAL checkpointing (but not the head GC, that is required).

Most likely, your server is just overloaded, and you are seeing non-graceful degradation here.

This is not really a bug in Prometheus, but we could improve logging to be clearer about what's going on here.

I would like to work on this issue. I am new to open source world. @beorn7 can you please guide me where and how logging should be implemented?
Thanks

Logging should just work in the same way as all the other logging. It's all over the code, you can take any as an example to see how it goes. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/073e93c76865ff39abccccd392d2111c56a3dc6d/tsdb/head.go#L809 , for example, is the line that has created one of the log entries in the original report above.

The more interesting question is on what condition we want to log what. @codesome might be able to give you a hint.
I am confused myself as to what we want to log here exactly :)

@codesome: If you don't know, then this might not have an easy solution after all…

You wrote:

> #7579 could partially help here to get rid of a loop of WAL checkpointing (but not the head GC, that is required).

I read this as "the head GC could run into a corner where it cannot finish with the given resources". The question is if there is a way to recognize that before simply OOMing and starting over again and again. Or even have a good guess at it based on some heuristics so that you can log something helpful like "Head GC is taking x minutes / y bytes / whatever. It might never finish. Consider deleting the WAL." (or whatever the appropriate measure would be).
The condition is if the GC+compaction takes longer than the minimum block size.

Now it makes sense to me. I would go with what Brian said and should be simple to check as compaction of Head and its GC happen in a single method `compactHead`. (@adrijshikhar: `head.Truncate` is the Head GC)
